elaine (AE): FYI — Customer BlueWave asked if we can run a 4-week air-gapped POC. They need: offline installer, signed bundles, SBOM, and a clear upgrade cadence. Also legal wants a short note on licensing for disconnected sites.
raj (SE): +1. Which edition are they evaluating? Hosted or Dedicated on prem?
elaine (AE): They want Redwood Private (on-prem) but with our private bundle (no outgoing calls). POC target is 2 racks, mixed GPUs.
sam (SRE): For air-gapped we provide an offline bundle + manifest. We need to confirm: do they accept delta patches or require full image each update?
elainE (AE): They prefer deltas to minimize bandwidth during onsite transfers, but security team might insist on full signed image every quarter. Still TBD.
victor (Eng): Technically we support delta patching via chunked bundles. The delta plan requires precomputed diff packages and a signed delta manifest. We need to surface required tooling on their side (rsync/scp or our USB ingestion tool).
raj (SE): Action: confirm customer can run our ingestion runner (linux x86_64) with root access. Also confirm HSM/KMS expectations — do they want us to sign with Redwood key or ship a signing tool?
sam (SRE): Security usually wants us to provide verifiable signatures and SBOM for each bundle. We can produce an SBOM (CycloneDX JSON) and sign the bundle with our key. If customer requires internal signing, we can provide a signing kit and instructions — but that adds legal paperwork.
elaine (AE): Legal asked: what licensing model applies to offline? Are POC credits separate or do they need a temporary reserved capacity contract? Pricing team needs a list of nodes + expected QPS to give a quote.
raj (SE): For POC we usually do a time-limited eval license (30–60 days) with limited support. If they want Dedicated/reserved, it's monthly commit. I can draft a POC quote once they confirm 2 racks / GPU types.
victor (Eng): Compatibility checklist we need from customer: OS image (ubuntu 22.04 or RHEL 9), container runtime (containerd), GPU drivers + expected CUDA/cuDNN versions, and network isolation details. If they are fully air-gapped we must provide offline cert rotation instructions.
sam (SRE): Example manifest snippet we send customers (we'll attach actual files in the bundle):
```
bundle_manifest: 
  version: 1
  bundles:
    - name: inference-runtime
      version: 2026.02.1
      sha256: abcdef...
    - name: model-shard-rr
      version: 7.4.0
      sha256: 123456...
  sbom: cycloneDX-20260201.json
  signature: bundle.sig
```
raj (SE): For upgrade cadence, recommend: POC -> weekly patch deltas (if accepted) or full images every 2 weeks, then production cadence 1x/month for security patches and 1x/quarter for major model/runtime upgrades. This keeps risk low.
elaine (AE): Customer security asked about rollback strategy if a delta fails. They want a deterministic rollback to the last known-good full bundle.
victor (Eng): We support atomic apply + fallback. The ingestion runner validates signatures, checks SBOM, runs preflight. If preflight fails we keep previous runtime and expose logs for forensics. We'll need to document failure codes.
sam (SRE): We'll produce a runbook for the POC (install -> validate -> ingest delta -> simulate failure -> rollback). I can own the runbook with Victor.
raj (SE): Quick pricing note: offline bundle delivery is considered a professional service add-on for air-gapped customers if more than 3 deliveries per year. Need sales ops signoff.
elaine (AE): Can someone confirm lead time for generating signed bundles and SBOM? Customer wants first bundle in 10 business days.
victor (Eng): Generating signed bundles + SBOM is ~2 days once we have validated model artifacts and runtime. Deltas take an extra day for diff generation and validation. Total 3 days after artifacts freeze.
raj (SE): I'll ask the customer to freeze artifacts and confirm GPUs today. Elaine, can you collect that and reply by EOD?
elaine (AE): On it. Also they asked about offline activation: need a one-time activation token vs. perpetual license? Legal prefers time-limited tokens for POC.
sam (SRE): For tokens we issue an offline activation file signed by our provisioning service. It can be time-limited. We need customer to supply node IDs (mac addresses / machine-ids).
raj (SE): Note for deployment: if they require FIPS/HSM for key storage, we need to confirm which KMS/HSM models they have. HSM-backed signing on their side is supported but will push more docs for legal.
deploy-bot: Bundle build job #43712 started by victor. Estimated time: 45m.
elaine (AE): Great. Final ask from customer: short one-pager explaining upgrade guarantees, rollback behavior, and expected downtime for upgrades (if any). Can we draft that?
victor (Eng): I'll draft the one-pager focusing on: no service downtime for small deltas (hot swap), planned 5–15m windows for major runtime upgrades with graceful draining, and full rollback plan.
sam (SRE): I'll add verification checklist and example commands for offline verification.
raj (SE): I'll add pricing footnote (POC eval license, pro-service for >3 deliveries/year).
elaine (AE): Perfect. Next steps: 1) I’ll collect GPU and artifact freeze by EOD. 2) Victor & Sam: runbook + one-pager draft by Thu. 3) Raj: POC quote + licensing note by Thu EOD. 4) Legal loop-in once artifacts frozen.
victor (Eng): ack.
sam (SRE): ack.
raj (SE): ack.
deploy-bot: Bundle build job #43712 completed successfully.
elaine (AE): thanks team — I'll update the customer and ping when artifacts are in.
